title: `CASE`, `IFF` and `COALESCE` are lazy; untaken errors never raise
verdict: branches see only their rows; constant errors in untaken branches do not raise
description: `CASE WHEN b = 0 THEN NULL ELSE a / b END` and `IFF(b = 0, NULL, a / b)` never divide by zero; `WHERE b <> 0 AND a / b > 1` and `COALESCE(a, 1 / b)` do not either. A constant error in an untaken branch (`CASE WHEN 1 = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 1 / 0 END`) does not raise at compile time.

sverify's SQL raises with a cast of a message to the result's type, which Snowflake reports with the message (`Numeric value 'sverify: integer overflow: …' is not recognized`); it raises only in its branch, and is NULL on a NULL dependency. Casts to `NUMBER`, `FLOAT`, `BOOLEAN`, `DATE`, `TIMESTAMP_NTZ` and `TIME` raise; to `VARCHAR` it does not, so a string's raise goes through `NUMBER` (this PR).
reference: A branch's expression is evaluated only on its rows: native.

provenance.checked_by: sverify_dev.probe_snowflake through the Snowflake CLI (Snowflake characterization session)

evidence.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN b = 0 THEN NULL ELSE a / b END FROM (VALUES (1, 0), (4, 2)) AS s(a, b)

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_snowflake` runs each query through `snow sql` (Snowflake CLI 3.32.1) on an X-Small warehouse, Snowflake 10.40.102, with the session's `TIMEZONE` set to UTC and `USE_CACHED_RESULT` off; every other parameter is the account's default, recorded in the header of probes.json (`WEEK_START` 0, `WEEK_OF_YEAR_POLICY` 0, `DEFAULT_NULL_ORDERING` LAST, `TIMESTAMP_TYPE_MAPPING` TIMESTAMP_NTZ). The inputs are literal `VALUES`, except the `sample-*` probes, which read TPC-H's LINEITEM (6,001,215 rows) in SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA.
